package: plug-in board, 2 × 15 pins (numbered as DIP-30: J1 = 1–15, J2 = 30–16), mini-USB

1.name: D1/TX
1.hint: ATmega328P PD1 (TXD); goes through 1 kΩ (RP1B) to the FT232RL RXD on the board

2.name: D0/RX
2.hint: ATmega328P PD0 (RXD); driven by the on-board FT232RL TXD through 1 kΩ (schematic RP1A) while the USB chip is powered

3.name: RESET
3.hint: reset, low active; 1 kΩ to +5V (schematic RP1D), reset button to GND, 100 nF from the FT232RL DTR# for the auto-reset

16.name: D13/SCK
16.hint: ATmega328P PB5 (SCK); on-board LED 'L' with 1 kΩ (RP2A) to GND

17.name: 3V3
17.hint: 3.3 V from the 3V3OUT of the FT232RL USB-serial chip (schematic); its current rating is in the FTDI datasheet (not read)

18.name: AREF
18.hint: ADC reference of the ATmega328P, 100 nF to GND on the board

25.name: A6
25.hint: ATmega328P ADC6: analog input only, no digital port

26.name: A7
26.hint: ATmega328P ADC7: analog input only, no digital port

27.name: +5V
27.hint: the 5 V rail: from VIN through the LM1117IMPX-5.0, or from USB through the MFFSMF050 polyfuse and the SS1P3L diode; the user manual also allows a regulated 5 V input here (pin 27)

28.name: RESET
28.hint: reset, low active; 1 kΩ to +5V (schematic RP1D), reset button to GND, 100 nF from the FT232RL DTR# for the auto-reset

30.name: VIN
30.hint: 7–15 V unregulated (user manual, pin 30) into the LM1117IMPX-5.0

hints: ATmega328P: the sum of IOH of C0–C5, D0–D4, ADC7, RESET and the sum of B0–B5, D5–D7, ADC6, XTAL1/2 each at most 150 mA; the sum of IOL of C0–C5, ADC6/7, of B0–B5, D5–D7, XTAL1/2 and of D0–D4, RESET each at most 100 mA (data sheet table 30-1 notes 3 and 4)
USB supply passes the MFFSMF050 polyfuse and the SS1P3L Schottky diode to +5V (schematic) – their ratings were not read

compliance.reach: Arduino: none of the SVHCs of the ECHA candidate list present at or above 0.1 % (user manual 7.2)
compliance.source: Arduino Nano User Manual, SKU A000005 (modified 30/10/2026): 7.2 RoHS 2/3, no exemptions claimed; REACH statement; board with ATmega328P and FT232RL, no transmitter (3.1 block diagram, schematic) – read 2026-10-31

sources: Arduino Nano User Manual, SKU A000005 (modified 30/10/2026) (docs.arduino.cc, read 2026-10-31): features (ATmega328 at 16 MHz, 7–15 V unregulated on pin 30, 5 V regulated on pin 27), 2.1 conservative thermal limits of the board –40 … 85 °C, 3.3 power tree (VIN through an LDO to 5 V), 7.2 RoHS/REACH; its pinout tables 5.1/5.2 contain errors (pin 1 '+3V3' described as '5V USB Power', pin 12 twice) – pin numbers taken from the schematic

Arduino Nano schematic NanoV3.3 (A000005-schematics.pdf, dated 23/01/19) (docs.arduino.cc, read 2026-10-31, as an image): J1 1–15 D1/TX, D0/RX, RESET, GND, D2–D12; J2 1–15 VIN, GND, RESET, +5V, A7–A0, AREF, 3V3, D13/SCK; IC2 LM1117IMPX-5.0 from VIN to +5V with 1 µF; F1 MFFSMF050 and D1 SS1P3L from USB VBUS to +5V; IC1 FT232RL (3V3OUT to 3V3, TXD/RXD through 1 kΩ to D0/D1, DTR# through 100 nF to RESET); RESET 1 kΩ (RP1D) to +5V and button to GND; LED L with 1 kΩ on D13; IC3 ATmega328P (328P-MUR) at 16 MHz, AREF with 100 nF

Microchip ATmega48A/PA/88A/PA/168A/PA/328/P megaAVR Data Sheet DS40002061B (ww1.microchip.com, read 2026-10-31): 29.1/30.1 absolute maximum (pins –0.5 V … VCC + 0.5 V, RESET up to 13 V, 6.0 V operating maximum, 40 mA DC per I/O pin, 200 mA through VCC and GND pins), table 30-1 (VIL 0.3 VCC, VIH 0.6 VCC at VCC 2.4–5.5 V; port sums), 29.3 speed grades (4 MHz at 1.8 V, 10 MHz at 2.7 V, 20 MHz at 4.5 V), tables 14-3/14-6/14-9 alternate port functions (TXD/RXD, OC0A/B, OC1A/B, OC2A/B, SS/MOSI/MISO/SCK, SDA/SCL, ADC0–5; ADC6/7 analog only), 24.6.1 ADC: 'optimized for analog signals with an output impedance of approximately 10 kΩ or less'
functions: Arduino pin → ATmega328P port from the schematic, the port's alternate functions from the data sheet; PWM instance = timer (one frequency per timer), line = compare output A/B
adc.range_v [0, 5.0]: 0 V … AVCC = +5V, the default reference – assumption: the firmware keeps the default reference (AREF pin without external reference)
the AVR VIH/VIL are from table 30-1 (–40 … 105 °C table; the –40 … 85 °C table did not extract as text)
pin v_max_v and gpio_v_max_v 5.5 V: VCC + 0.5 V at VCC 5 V (abs. max); RESET held to the same 5.5 V although the AVR allows 13 V on RESET (the board joins it to +5V through 1 kΩ)
VIN v_max_v 15 V and vin_min_v/vin_max_v 7–15 V: the user manual's range; the LM1117's own ratings were not read
notes: Bought board without an LCSC number, keyed by its manufacturer part number (handbook 4: a part bought from another distributor; 4.5 bought boards) – a component names it with part = A000005 and bom: false. footprint and order are not filled (see verified.open).

verified.datasheet: Arduino Nano User Manual, SKU A000005 (modified 30/10/2026); Arduino Nano schematic NanoV3.3 (A000005-schematics.pdf, dated 23/01/19); Microchip ATmega48A/PA/88A/PA/168A/PA/328/P megaAVR Data Sheet DS40002061B
checked: header pins J1/J2 and the DIP-30 numbering against the schematic and the user manual's pin 27 (+5V) and pin 30 (VIN)
power path: VIN → LM1117IMPX-5.0 → +5V; USB → MFFSMF050 → SS1P3L → +5V; 3V3 from the FT232RL
ATmega328P absolute maximum: VCC + 0.5 V per pin, 40 mA per pin, 200 mA VCC/GND; VIH 0.6 VCC, VIL 0.3 VCC
speed grades 4/10/20 MHz at 1.8/2.7/4.5 V; the board runs at 16 MHz
alternate functions of D0–D13 and A0–A7
RoHS (no exemptions) and REACH statement of the user manual
open: footprint: no EasyEDA footprint name chosen for the plug-in board (header pair 2 × 15, 2.54 mm) – to be set with the project's footprint
order: no distributor order code read (PARTS.supplier warns about a bom: false part without one)

LM1117IMPX-5.0 (TI datasheet not read): dropout_v, iq_a, rth_ja_k_per_w and tj_max_c of the on-board LDO – LIM.t has no temperature item without them; the simulation's default dropout 0.3 V is lower than an LM1117's
core current (i_core_a): the ATmega328P table gives 9 mA max at 8 MHz/5 V only; FT232RL and LEDs add to it – the simulation's default applies
MFFSMF050 polyfuse and SS1P3L diode ratings not read
the user manual's pinout tables 5.1/5.2 contradict the schematic (pin 1 '+3V3'/'5V USB Power', pin 12 twice) – the schematic is followed
